Scene 03

X-FILES OFFICE

Fox Mulder

Divorced. No children. He came to the u.s. From uzbekistan during perestroika. He failed to mention on his I.n.s. Application... That he spent the better part of his 20s in an insane asylum.

Dana Scully

Fox Mulder

You thought all they produced were great hockey players. The crimes took place during a three-year period. All the victims male, age 17 to 25.

Dana Scully

Was there a signature or a defining m.o.?

Fox Mulder

Well, according to the m.e., there was no evidence of any sexual assault. Death was caused by massive blood loss due to facial mutilation. He also reported that the wound pattern on all the victims was identical. It's all there on page three.

[ flipping pages ]

Dana Scully

"both eyes punctured. Signature gashes from the corners of the mouth to the ears." the level of violence and overkill here... Would suggest the work of a very angry individual.

Fox Mulder

Or individuals, if you count the spirit Mostow says possessed him during the murders.

Dana Scully

Possession is a common claim by criminals who have dissociative disorders. It's how they distance themselves from their actions.

Fox Mulder

That was the operational opinion until last night, when a 19-year-old male... Was found dead six Miles from here with an identical set of facial wounds.

Dana Scully

A copycat?

Fox Mulder

According to assistant director Skinner, who asked us to look into this, the details of the mutilations were never released. Only members of the crime team would have had that information. And Mostow's been in custody for five days.

Scene 10

LIBRARY

[ Mulder thinking ]

Fox Mulder

The name is from the french "gargouille"-- the name of a medieval dragon which prowled the river seine, whose horrible image became a symbol of the souls of the condemned turned to stone... Or of the devils and demons of the underworld spared eternal damnation. The embodiment of the lesser forces of the universe... Who inspired dread and the threat of our own damnation. Ushers into hell or into the realm of our own dark fears and imagination. For over 1,200 years, the grotesque image has found its expression... In stone, clay, wood, oil, and charcoal-- born again and again, as if resurrecting itself by its own will... Through tortured human expression. Almost as if it existed, haunting men inwardly so that it might haunt mankind for eternity... As it must've haunted john Mostow. But what impulses moved him to kill? Could this be the same dark force at work, its ultimate expression the destruction of the flesh, of the very hand that creates it? Is this evil something born in each of us, crouching in the shadow of every human soul, waiting to emerge, a monster that violates our bodies and twists our will to do its bidding? [ continues thinking ] is this the monster called madness?

Bill Patterson

[ gasps ] they're closing up in a few minutes. So, is this how you're looking for the second killer? Tell me, Mulder, what do you really expect to find here?

Fox Mulder

I'm not sure yet.

Bill Patterson

But you must have some idea, some kind of theory.

Fox Mulder

I've got a few theories. I'm trying to stitch them together right now.

Bill Patterson

With your face stuck in a library book?

Fox Mulder

You said it yourself. If you want to know the artist, look at the art. I'm finally agreeing with you.

Bill Patterson

I know where you're going with this, Mulder, because I've been there myself-- so I can tell you you're wasting your time.

Fox Mulder

Maybe you could tell me why this man was compelled to draw... And sculpt the same face again and again, why he's still doing it now.

Bill Patterson

Because he's insane. This is nothing but the scrawling of a madman.

Fox Mulder

He said this thing wants to see its own reflection.

Bill Patterson

Mostow has said everything but what I need to hear-- the name of his accomplice.

Fox Mulder

Unless he's telling the truth.

Bill Patterson

About being possessed? I have to tell you. I am really disappointed in you.

Fox Mulder

Well, I wouldn't want to disappoint you by not disappointing you.

Bill Patterson

Clearly, I was mistaken.
